articles.summary: Many labs rely on spreadsheets to connect data from outside partners, studies, instruments, and internal teams. Over time, those spreadsheets often take on work that belongs in software: mapping sample IDs, standardizing units, tracking exceptions, deciding which results need review, and preparing final reports. This article explains why that happens, why generic lab software can struggle with highly specific workflows, and how a connected data foundation can give AI the context it needs to support lab operations. It also introduces Scispot Jazz, an approach designed to help labs build purpose-built applications around the way they already work.
articles.title: When Your Lab Spreadsheet Starts Acting Like Custom Software

articles.summary: For decades, labs have adapted their work to fit the limits of software. Scientists turned complex processes into forms, fields, fixed workflows, and manual workarounds because traditional systems could only understand structured inputs. AI creates an opportunity to reverse that relationship. But AI still needs context. It needs to understand a lab’s data, workflows, rules, and history before it can be useful. Scispot Jazz builds on the Scispot Digital Brain to help labs turn the way they actually work into purpose-built software. The goal is simple: software that can better reflect the workflow, review process, and operational reality of each lab.

articles.summary: Every lab has workflows that look unusual from the outside. A custom CRO data intake process, a QC review step, a trusted calculation, or an exception process may not apply to every lab. But it may be central to how your team protects data quality, moves work forward, and gets reliable answers. For years, these workflows were often treated as “edge cases.” In large software products, that was understandable. A feature built for one team can add complexity for thousands of other users. But for the lab that created the workflow, it is rarely an edge case. It is often the result of years of scientific judgment and operational learning. Scispot helps labs bring these workflows into their lab operating system. With Scispot’s Digital Brain as the foundation for lab data, relationships, workflows, rules, and history, Jazz gives teams a way to turn their specific last-mile requirements into purpose-built applications. That can include CRO workflows, QC reviews, reports, exception handling, sample traceability, data review, and automation.
